applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: OECD Multilateral Convention on Mutual Administrative Assistance

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Alberta Business Corporations Act, RSA 2000, c B-9; Canada Business Corporations Act, RSC 1985, c C-44 (if federal); Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, SC 2000, c 17 (PCMLTFA); Criminal Code of Canada, RSC 1985, c C-46; Alberta Information and Privacy Act (for registry access); relevant regulations under the Canada Business Corporations Act respecting beneficial ownership registers.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of passport of each individual director, officer, and ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport issuing authority; notarization by a licensed notary public in country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Canada is party to the Hague Conference); for non-Hague jurisdictions, consular legalization through Canadian Embassy/Consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Incumbency for any corporate shareholder or corporate director
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registry or government authority in jurisdiction of incorporation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter confirming identity and financial probity for each UBO and director
Corporate resolution or board consent authorizing formation of the Alberta ULC and appointment of legal agents, if an entity is the shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate records office of the foreign parent entity

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of registered address of each UBO and director (utility bill or official bank statement)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, officers, shareholders, and ultimate beneficial owners against the Office of Financial Sanctions enforcement lists, OFAC SDN list, UN Security Council Consolidated List, Canadian Special Economic Measures Act and regulations, and FINTRAC guidance relating to politically exposed persons (PEPs). Enhanced due diligence required for non-resident or corporate shareholders, high-risk jurisdictions, or transactions involving standby letters of credit. Screening must be completed before incorporating and refreshed at filing of the annual return.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry (via authorized service providers and the official registry system)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be available in English or French or a combination thereof, with permissible numerals and punctuation in accordance with Alberta Business Corporations Act regulations. A proposed name containing a word in a language other than English or French, or a phrase that is not correctly transcribed in the Latin alphabet, may be required to be transliterated by statutory declaration; the NUANS search report must be produced for name reservation.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Or any word suggesting professional practice or regulated activity without prior ministerial or governing body approval
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, applicant may file a written reconsideration request with the Director of Corporate Registries within 30 days of rejection, specifying the grounds for reversal; if the reconsideration is denied, the applicant may appeal to the Court of King's Bench of Alberta under the Alberta Business Corporations Act within 30 days of the denial. Re-submission of a new name reservation with a fresh NUANS search is also available as a parallel remedy.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office arrangements are generally permissible for the registered office address provided a physical address in Alberta is designated and capable of accepting service of process. However, for the marine bunkering and refueling business, the Alberta registered office is not accepted as an operational facility; physical commercial premises, environmental approvals, and Port Authority authorizations are required for actual bunkering operations.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low for the registered office only (estimated 5% annual probability of desk-based verification); moderate for operational bunkering sites (estimated 15-20% annual probability of site inspection by Transport Canada, environmental regulators, or port authorities, particularly for fuel-handling infrastructure)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for standard ULC incorporation by an Alberta law firm

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Alberta registered agent / corporate service provider

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Beneficial ownership register setup and UBO confirmation filings
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Combined statutory filing fee and professional fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Compliance review of PEP/OFAC/UN screening and AML/CFT pre-incorporation due diligence

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c. B-9, sections 1.1 to 1.4 (Unlimited Liability Corporations)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital requirement for ULCs in Alberta; directors must ensure sufficient capitalization for operations and solvency

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Access the Alberta Corporate Registry website at corporate-registry.alberta.ca, perform a name search to confirm availability, submit a name reservation application if desired, and pay the associated fee.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If name is unavailable, select an alternative name and re-submit after verification

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft Articles of Incorporation specifying the corporation as Unlimited Liability Corporation, include details on share structure, directors, registered office, and incorporators. Have incorporators sign and date the articles.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If deficiencies noted, amend and resubmit promptly

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry via online portal or mail
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upload the completed Articles of Incorporation and supporting documents to the online portal or submit by mail to the Corporate Registry in Edmonton. Pay the filing fee.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If application is queried, provide additional information or documentation within the specified timeframe

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval, receive the Certificate of Incorporation electronically or by mail, confirming the corporation's legal existence.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If rejected, appeal or correct issues and reapply

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Transport Canada Marine Safety and Alberta Environment and Parks
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Marine Fuel Bunkering and Lubricant Replenishment Permit

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Adherence to Alberta Wastewater and Air Quality Standards; no unauthorized discharge of hydrocarbons or lubricants; VOC emissions controlled per Alberta Regulation 27/2020

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification and inspection by Alberta Fire and Emergency Services; structural load assessments for fuel storage facilities; workplace clearance under the Alberta Occupational Health and Safety Act

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA), Business Registration Online (BRO) portal via https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency.html; Alberta has no provincial sales tax authority and the province imposes no PST, so the federal GST/HST program account is the sole indirect-tax registration. For marine bunkering, the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) administers customs export reporting and the federal excise duty framework under the Excise Act, 2001.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned Alberta ULC must: (1) incorporate or register extra-provincially under the Alberta Business Corporations Act to obtain an Alberta corporate access number; (2) apply to the CRA for a Business Number (BN) by filing Form RC1 or using Business Registration Online, specifying the GST/HST program account (RT0001); (3) designate a Canadian representative (Form RC59) if the ULC is a non-resident entity without a permanent establishment in Canada; (4) enroll for direct deposit (RC3661). The 9-digit BN plus two-letter program identifier constitutes the statutory TIN / VAT ID for all federal tax filings. Non-resident ULCs may also be required to register with CBSA for a carrier/client identifier coincident with Customs Self-Assessment.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation – an Alberta ULC is a taxable Canadian corporation resident in Alberta under the Income Tax Act; it is subject to federal and Alberta corporate income tax on worldwide income at the entity level. Pass-through treatment is not available domestically; only the U.S. parent may, for U.S. federal tax purposes, elect disregarded-entity or partnership status via IRC §301.7701-3 check-the-box, a foreign classification that the CRA disregards for GST/HST and income tax, resulting in hybrid-mismatch exposure having to be managed.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No Canadian check-the-box or general flow-through election exists for a ULC. The only relevant statutory elections are: (i) the U.S. check-the-box election on IRS Form 8832 for the ULC (flow-through/disregarded/partnership treatment) with treaty-side relief considered under Canada-U.S. Income Tax Convention Article IV(7) (fiscally transparent entity); (ii) the GST/HST joint election under Excise Tax Act s. 273 for closely related GST registrants to consolidate returns; (iii) the Unified Tax Reform hybrid-mismatch election mechanisms under Income Tax Act ss. 211.2–211.9, which recharacterize the ULC's transactions with foreign shareholders to prevent deduction/non-inclusion outcomes. A ULC with only non-resident shareholders must also attend to the special conduit-distribution rules governing deemed dividends (ss. 84(1) and 84(7)) on redemption or windup.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax) – Alberta rate is composed exclusively of the federal component (GST) because Alberta levies no provincial sales tax. Marine bunker fuel is additionally subject to federal excise duty under the Excise Act, 2001 (about CAD 0.04/L for diesel) unless the fuel is shipped for international commercial navigation, in which case duty-free or refund mechanics may apply via the CBSA.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 – the small-supplier threshold measured on worldwide taxable supplies; a non-resident ULC making taxable supplies in Canada in the course of a commercial activity must register once the threshold is exceeded, while voluntary registration is allowable to claim input tax credits on Canadian expenditures. Registration is likewise mandatory for zero-rated bunkering suppliers that cannot demonstrate small-supplier status and whose customers require a GST-registered invoice.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: None – Canada imposes no mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, no API-based e-invoice clearance, and no digital stamping requirement for GST/HST. The Pan-Canadian (PEPPOL) e-invoicing framework is voluntary for private-sector transactions, and the CRA only mandates electronic filing of GST/HST returns for registrants above prescribed thresholds. The invoice must nevertheless satisfy ETA s. 169/basic book-and-record requirements (s. 286) with a six-year retention period and show GST registration number on supply invoices.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies under Schedule VI to the Excise Tax Act in two relevant limbs: (a) goods shipped by the supplier to a destination outside Canada and exported as part of the supply contract (Schedule VI, Part I, s. 1); and (b) property and services supplied to the operator of an international commercial marine vessel, including bunker fuel, lubricants, water and ship stores supplied while the vessel is engaged in international voyage operations (Schedule VI, Part I, s. 23). The substantive test for bunkering is that the vessel is operated by a non-resident or, if resident, the fuel is realistically destined to be consumed on an international sailing leg outside Canada. Documentary evidence must prove physical export or international-sea consumption and receipt of consideration.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration filed electronically through the CBSA Canadian Export Reporting System (CERS) / Export Declaration (replacing the former B13A) or the applicable barge/vessel manifest where marine export procedures apply
Ocean Bill of Lading or marine Bunker Delivery Receipt (BDN) evidencing the international vessel's name, IMO number, port of delivery, voyage itinerary and quantity/quality of fuel delivered
Commercial invoice and bunker sale contract referencing the ISIC 5222 / NAICS 488390 activity and showing the 0% GST rate
Inward foreign-currency remittance evidence – SWIFT MT103, bank transfer entry or foreign exchange summary – demonstrating receipt of export consideration from a non-resident party
Where applicable, excise-duty-paid records and the CBSA marine vessel fuel refund or duty-free entry documentation supporting international commercial navigation
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The CRA routinely audits marine bunkering zero-rating claims; failure to substantiate the export/consumption and foreign payment within the evidentiary window results in reassessment adding 5% GST on the sale, plus prescribed arrears interest (ETA s. 280) and, in the case of false or grossly negligent statements, civil penalties under ETA s. 283 (up to the greater of CAD 250 and 40% of the tax sought to be evaded for knowing misrepresentation). Knowingly evading GST is a criminal offence under ETA s. 327 with fines, on indictment, of 50%–200% of the tax evaded and imprisonment up to 5 years. Input tax credits claimed on bunkering purchases can be recaptured under ETA s. 296, and director/shareholder liability for unrecovered GST can be asserted under ETA s. 323. For ULC structures, CRA may further apply the general anti-avoidance rule (Income Tax Act s. 245) and hybrid-mismatch rules where the foreign parent treats the Alberta ULC as transparent while the bunkering revenue is not effectively included in Canadian taxable income.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada. Canada has no standalone foreign exchange administration imposing general exchange controls. Financial institution prudential supervision is principally administered by the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions, while anti-money-laundering compliance is administered by the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar is generally fully convertible for current-account and capital-account transactions. Canada does not generally impose capital controls, mandatory repatriation of foreign currency, or restrictions on remitting lawful dividends, interest, royalties, loan proceeds, or sale proceeds. Remittances remain subject to corporate-law authorization, solvency requirements, applicable withholding tax, transfer-pricing rules, beneficial-ownership verification, sanctions screening, anti-money-laundering controls, tax reporting, and bank documentation. An Alberta unlimited liability corporation may create additional parent-company tax classification and withholding-tax analysis, particularly where a non-Canadian shareholder treats the entity as fiscally transparent.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada does not impose a general statutory requirement to surrender export proceeds to a Canadian bank, repatriate export receipts within a prescribed period, or convert a mandatory percentage of export receipts into Canadian dollars. Export proceeds may generally remain in foreign-currency accounts or be converted at the holder's discretion. Transactions remain subject to sanctions, anti-terrorist-financing requirements, customs and export-control rules, tax reporting, bank transaction monitoring, and record-retention obligations. Financial institutions may request commercial invoices, bills of lading, vessel information, counterparty details, and evidence of the underlying bunkering transaction before releasing or converting funds.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium for payment initiation and foreign-exchange execution; Low for replacing a Canadian operating bank account. Canada does not use a single European-style electronic-money-institution licensing regime. A foreign digital EMI generally cannot accept deposits from the public or provide unrestricted payment-account services in Canada without an applicable Canadian authorization, registration, exemption, or regulated-bank partnership. A payment service provider that falls within Canada's Retail Payment Activities Act framework may require Bank of Canada registration and must satisfy operational-risk, safeguarding, incident-reporting, and funds-handling requirements. Foreign EMI balances may also be unsuitable for capital contributions, payroll, trust-like client funds, or high-value marine-fuel settlements. Use a Canadian federally or provincially regulated financial institution as the primary account bank and treat an offshore EMI as a supplemental rail only after legal, sanctions, settlement, safeguarding, and counterparty review.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Canadian banks may permit remote onboarding for an Alberta corporation, including digitally executed applications and video identification, but this is discretionary and transaction-risk dependent. Physical attendance is not universally mandated by statute. Banks may require notarized or certified corporate documents, in-person identification, a Canadian business address, Canadian resident signing authority or relationship manager, video interviews with directors and beneficial owners, and enhanced due diligence where ownership, control, source of funds, foreign tax residency, vessel activity, or expected transaction flows are international. Remote onboarding is less likely to be approved where the ULC has non-resident directors, no Canadian operating footprint, complex ownership, or expected high-value cross-border payments.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inability to identify and verify every beneficial owner, controller, director, authorized signatory, or intermediate holding entity of the ULC.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified articles and corporate registry extracts; current register of directors and shareholders; ownership chart through all intermediate entities to natural persons; passports and proof of address; tax-residency self-certifications; corporate resolutions; declarations of control; and an independent ownership database report.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident ownership combined with a newly formed Alberta ULC, limited Canadian substance, or unclear commercial rationale for using an unlimited liability entity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board-approved Canadian business plan; Alberta registered-office and operating-address evidence; service-provider, terminal, supplier, and customer contracts; employee or agent information; projected Canadian revenues and expenses; explanation of ULC legal and tax classification; organization chart; and written tax advice addressing shareholder and cross-border consequences.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Marine bunkering payments involving vessels, charterers, brokers, shipowners, ports, terminals, or counterparties connected with sanctioned or higher-risk jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Vessel name, IMO number, flag, ownership and management records; charter-party or supply contract; port call and delivery details; bill of lading or bunker delivery note; customer and supplier sanctions-screening results; AIS or voyage evidence where available; end-use certification; beneficial-owner checks; and documented escalation procedures.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large, rapid, or circular transfers inconsistent with the stated bunkering business, including third-party payments, pass-through funds, cash deposits, or payments from unrelated affiliates.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: 12-month cash-flow forecast; transaction-level payment matrix; approved counterparty list; invoice-to-payment reconciliation; treasury policy; intercompany agreements; loan or capital-contribution agreements; source-of-funds and source-of-wealth evidence; dual-approval controls; and written explanation for any third-party settlement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign capital injection without clear classification as equity, shareholder loan, or other permitted funding, or without evidence of the remitting party's authority.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Shareholder or board resolutions; subscription agreement or loan agreement; capitalization table; beneficial-owner confirmation; remitter bank details; audited or management financial statements; source-of-funds evidence; tax analysis; transfer-pricing support for related-party debt; and payment instructions matching the legal documentation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected foreign-currency volume, hedging activity, or trade-finance usage materially exceeds the business plan or lacks a documented operating purpose.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Currency exposure policy; monthly currency forecast; purchase and sale contracts; hedge-ratio methodology; approved derivatives counterparties; ISDA and collateral documentation; authorized trader matrix; derivative valuation and reporting procedures; and management-approved limits.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Adverse media, regulatory enforcement, corruption allegations, environmental incidents, fuel-quality disputes, or unexplained intermediary commissions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Compliance questionnaire; litigation and regulatory search results; anti-bribery policy; sanctions and export-control policy; commission agreements; beneficial-owner certifications; third-party due-diligence reports; incident register; remediation evidence; and legal opinions where allegations are unresolved.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route funds through the ULC's Canadian bank account using a SWIFT wire or other bank-approved international transfer. Identify the legal nature of the payment accurately as paid-up capital, share subscription proceeds, shareholder loan, or intercompany funding; Canada does not prescribe a universal foreign-exchange purpose-code system for ordinary corporate capital inflows. Include the ULC legal name, Alberta registration number, account details, remitter identity, beneficial-owner information, agreement or resolution reference, and a clear payment narrative. The receiving bank may request source-of-funds evidence, source-of-wealth information, audited or management accounts, subscription or loan documents, tax-residency data, and sanctions-screening information. Avoid undisclosed nominee funding, third-party remitters, netting, or commingling of capital with customer collections. Record the receipt in the corporate books and reconcile it to the capitalization or debt schedule. Consider Canadian withholding tax, thin-capitalization, transfer-pricing, debt-equity, and shareholder-benefit consequences before using shareholder loans.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use bank-originated SWIFT MT103 or its current ISO 20022 equivalent for ordinary supplier, vessel, terminal, lubricant, and service payments. Match each payment to an approved counterparty, commercial invoice, purchase order or bunkering contract, bunker delivery note, vessel and port details, and sanctions-screening record. For documentary or higher-risk settlements, use a commercial documentary letter of credit, standby letter of credit, or bank guarantee subject to agreed UCP 600, ISP98, or URDG 758 rules, as applicable. Confirm issuing-bank and confirming-bank sanctions exposure, reimbursement arrangements, discrepancy procedures, expiry dates, governing law, and collateral requirements. Use CAD or a contractual settlement currency with documented FX conversion and beneficiary verification. Direct debit, wires, ACH, EFT, and correspondent-bank rails should be limited to approved counterparties and subject to dual authorization, payment screening, callback controls, segregation of duties, and invoice-to-payment reconciliation.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable foreign-exchange forwards with a regulated bank or eligible derivatives dealer, used to hedge documented CAD, USD, EUR, or other operating exposures and supported by a treasury limit, maturity, and settlement schedule.

Non-deliverable forwards for currencies where market or regulatory conditions make physical delivery impracticable, subject to counterparty eligibility, local-currency settlement rules, sanctions screening, and derivatives documentation.

Foreign-currency swaps and cross-currency swaps for matching the currency, duration, and interest profile of shareholder loans, trade finance, or recurring operating cash flows, subject to ISDA documentation, collateral terms, valuation controls, and applicable Canadian derivatives reporting or provincial securities requirements.

Foreign-exchange options or option collars, where appropriate, for downside protection with defined premium, exercise, accounting, and counterparty limits; speculative or unapproved naked positions should be prohibited by treasury policy.

For all instruments, maintain documented commercial exposure, board-approved authority, counterparty limits, independent valuation, confirmations, accounting treatment, collateral monitoring, and periodic effectiveness review. Canadian banks may impose product-specific suitability, disclosure, margin, reporting, and documentation requirements.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the annual anniversary of incorporation or registration in Alberta
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file places the ULC in registry default; continued delinquency for 12 months may trigger administrative dissolution, requiring court-ordered reinstatement or fresh incorporation. Additional late filing and restoration fees may apply.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (Federal and Alberta Corporate Income Tax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than 6 months after the end of the taxation year, including the Alberta corporate tax component administered under the T2 regime
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty equals 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per full month of delinquency, maximum 12 months, with a minimum penalty of $100 CAD. Gross negligence and repeated failure to file may invoke CRA enforcement, asset liens, and director liability.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A private, non-distributing Alberta ULC is not required by the Alberta Business Corporations Act to appoint an auditor solely based on revenue, assets, or employees. An audit becomes compulsory if the corporation is a distributing or reporting issuer, if shareholders who collectively hold at least 10% of issued shares requisition an audit, or if a marine bunkering license, port authority, or lender mandates audited financial statements as a condition of the operating license or credit facility. In the absence of such triggers, shareholders may unanimously waive the audit for that fiscal year.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS for publicly accountable or distributing corporations; otherwise the Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE), CPA Canada Handbook Part II, is the applicable Canadian GAAP framework for a private ULC. Tax-basis financial statements may be prepared for ancillary purposes but are not a substitute for ASPE or IFRS statutory financial statements.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: There is no annual stand-alone UBO filing for an Alberta ULC. The ULC must maintain a current internal register of members reflecting legal ownership, and any share transfer must be recorded in the corporate registers by amendment of the Register of Members. The Alberta annual return confirms registered office and director information only. Beneficial ownership details are not submitted annually to Service Alberta unless the entity becomes a reporting issuer or an applicable federal beneficial ownership registry requirement applies.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 23.0% (15.0% federal Part I general rate + 8.0% Alberta general corporate income tax rate)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holidays. A qualifying Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) may use the small-business deduction to achieve an 11% combined rate on the first CAD 500,000 of active business income; an Alberta ULC that is owned or controlled by a non-resident parent generally does not qualify. Preferential deductions include accelerated capital cost allowance (CCA) for marine vessels, storage tanks, and terminal equipment; SR&ED investment tax credits if eligible.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return; filed electronically with the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) via My Business Account, EFIL, or approved tax software portals.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due six months after the taxation year-end. Tax balance payable within two months of year-end (three months for qualifying CCPCs). A non-resident ULC with a Canadian permanent establishment follows the same filing and payment deadlines.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue from marine fuel, bunkering, lubricant replenishment, and ancillary offshore supply services before deducting any costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only revenue attributable to a Canadian permanent establishment; convert foreign-currency amounts to Canadian dollars using CRA daily exchange rates.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible business expenses: bunker fuel procurement, terminal and barge CCA, crew wages, insurance, port charges, environmental compliance, and arm's-length third-party storage.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Expenses must be reasonable and incurred to earn Canadian source business income; apply arm's-length allocations for head-office overhead and intercompany charges.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Business income after all deductions and non-capital loss carryovers.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident ULC, taxable income includes only Canadian-source income, not world income; non-capital losses may carry back three years and forward twenty years.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: T2 Box 300 - Federal Part I Tax
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Federal tax at 15% general corporate rate, reduced by applicable investment tax credits and foreign tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporations are not eligible for the federal small business deduction; treaty benefits must be claimed through the applicable Canada tax treaty.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allocation of taxable income to the Alberta permanent establishment under the Alberta corporate income tax regime; Alberta general rate of 8% applies.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If a permanent establishment exists in Alberta, allocate income using CRA/Alberta prescribed allocation rules; a non-resident with no PE has no Alberta corporate tax exposure.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per full month, up to 12 months. For knowing or negligent failure, penalty increases to 10% plus 2% per month, up to 24 months. CRA also charges daily compound interest on unpaid tax at the prescribed rate. Alberta may impose parallel penalties for its provincial portion.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Alberta Corporate Income Tax Return (AT1); filed through the Alberta Tax and Revenue Administration online portal, or via CRA developed e-file software where Alberta schedules are transmitted together with the federal T2.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due six months after the taxation year-end; Alberta corporate tax payment due within two months of year-end (three months for qualifying CCPCs).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Federal taxable income adjusted for Alberta-specific provincial allocations and additions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents allocate taxable income to Alberta only to the extent attributable to a permanent establishment located in Alberta.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: AT1 Part 2 - Alberta Tax Before Credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Compute Alberta corporate tax at 8% on the allocated Alberta taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No Alberta branch tax is imposed separately; the 8% rate applies to PE-allocated income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claim Alberta non-capital loss carryovers and prior-year adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents may claim carryovers deducted from PE-allocated income subject to the twenty-year forward period.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Alberta levies a late filing penalty of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per month, up to 12 months; repeated or negligent failure attracts 10% + 2% per month, up to 24 months. Compounded interest accrues at the Alberta prescribed rate.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% Part XIII withholding tax on gross dividends paid by an Alberta ULC or any Canadian-resident corporation to a non-resident beneficial owner, absent treaty reduction.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim treaty relief, the non-resident beneficial owner must complete and provide Federal Form NR301 (Declaration of Eligibility for Benefits Under a Tax Treaty) to the Canadian payer before the payment is made, together with a valid tax residence certificate (TRC) if requested. The payer then withholds at the treaty rate: under the Canada-US treaty, dividends are reduced to 5% if the corporate beneficial owner owns at least 10% of the voting stock; otherwise 15%. If full 25% was withheld because treaty evidence was not submitted, the non-resident may apply to CRA for refund under Form NR7-R with supporting TRC.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory domestic rate: 25% on interest and 25% on royalties paid to non-residents, subject to specific statutory exemptions for arm's-length interest on certain obligations. Under Canada-US DTA or most OECD-compatible DTA treaties: interest to a beneficial owner who is a resident of the treaty country is generally exempt from Canadian withholding (0%); royalties are generally reduced to 10%, with certain artistic/culture royalties at 0%.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Contemporaneous Canadian transfer pricing documentation is mandatory when the aggregate annual value of related-party cross-border transactions (e.g., intercompany fuel purchases, management fees, or vessel leases) exceeds CAD 1,000,000. A Country-by-Country Report and Master File are required for multinational groups with annual consolidated revenue of at least CAD 750,000,000.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada and Alberta do not maintain standalone Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) of the UAE/GCC type. However, CRA uses the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR), corporate-residence tests, and treaty-benefit rules to deny tax benefits where an Alberta ULC is used as a shell or conduit without real economic substance. The ULC must have substantive board decision-making, employees, physical premises, invoicing, and risk-bearing functions in Alberta for vessel bunkering and refueling operations; otherwise treaty entitlement is exposed and the entity may be recharacterized.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate omission of cash marine-fuel sales, creation of false bunkering delivery reports, use of untraceable third-party payments, or suppression of international vessel refueling invoices from the ULC's books.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Gross negligence penalty of 50% of the amount of tax sought to be evaded; interest accrual; criminal prosecution under Income Tax Act s.239 with fines up to 200% of the evaded tax and imprisonment up to five years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false returns or direct concealment can be assessed for unremitted Part XIII or payroll taxes under s.227.1; criminal convictions can trigger travel bans, extradition requests, personal civil restitution, and imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using an Alberta ULC as a bare invoice intermediary with no substantive fuel-storage assets, employees, vessel activities, or risk management, while all real control and business functions remain outside Canada solely to access the Canada-US DTA and the low Alberta tax rate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Application of GAAR to deny the tax benefit; recharacterization of cross-border payments as dividends or royalties; enhanced 25% GAAR penalty on the denied benefit (for transactions after relevant amendment); Part XIII withholding reassessed at 25% plus interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: CRA may disregard the corporate status and trace liability to the controlling person; directors who knowingly participate in the sham may be named in civil fraud proceedings, subjected to asset-seizure orders, and prevented from leaving the country in serious tax-recovery proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Underpricing bunker fuel sold to related foreign ship operators, overpaying foreign related suppliers, allocating excessive head-office fees to Canada, or intentionally failing to prepare contemporaneous CUP/TNMM evidence for intercompany marine-fuel transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Transfer pricing penalty equal to 10% of the net adjustment for transfer-pricing misstatements (ITA s.247(3)); CRA can reassess at arm's-length prices and charge interest from the original due date; facilities may be subject to garnishment for unpaid balances.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are not automatically assessed for the TP penalty, but if the mispricing results in deemed payments subject to Part XIII withholding (e.g., deemed interest/royalty), directors may become personally liable for unremitted withholding tax; criminal charges can follow where false invoices are certified.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting suspicious high-risk telegraphic transfers, standby LC draw-downs, or cash deposits above CAD 10,000 from flags-of-convenience vessel interests without filing FINTRAC reports; fueling vessels linked to sanctioned jurisdictions; issuing false bills of lading to disguise the origin of funds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative monetary penalties under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act: up to CAD 500,000 for a first offence and CAD 1,000,000 for a subsequent offence; criminal money-laundering prosecution under the Criminal Code carries up to ten years imprisonment; sanctions violations under the UN Act trigger asset forfeiture and fines.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers are personally liable where they knowingly directed or failed to report suspicious transactions; they face criminal conviction, personal asset forfeiture, travel restrictions in extradition/sanctions cases, and permanent debarment from Canadian financial services sectors.
